id.label: Tile (county FIPS - number within the county)

texture.label: Soil textural class, 0-25 cm
texture.source: ISSR-800 (SSURGO/STATSGO, USDA-NRCS and UC Davis), 800 m pixels inside the tile

texture_pct.label: Share of the tile in its most frequent textural class

paws_mm.label: Plant available water storage, soil profile

wheat_pct.label: Winter wheat share of the land
wheat_pct.source: USDA-NASS Cropland Data Layer, mean of 2016 to 2023, 1-km cells

pawc_mm.label: Plant available water capacity, 0-120 cm
pawc_mm.source: kansas-1km total available water (0-60 cm, 1-km cells), doubled for 0-120 cm

plant_doy.label: Typical planting date (middle of the window)

season_days.label: Typical growing season, planting to harvest

seasonal.season: typical planting date to typical harvest date of each tile, named by the harvest year

variables.name: pr
variables.label: Precipitation
variables.definition: Total precipitation from the typical planting date to the typical harvest date of the tile (Crop calendar).

variables.name: fallow_pr
variables.label: Fallow precipitation
variables.definition: Total precipitation of the summer fallow before the season: from the day after the typical harvest date to the day before the typical planting date of the tile (Crop calendar).

variables.name: eto
variables.label: Reference evapotranspiration
variables.definition: Total grass reference evapotranspiration (gridMET) from the typical planting date to the typical harvest date of the tile (Crop calendar).

variables.name: water_deficit
variables.label: Atmospheric water deficit
variables.definition: Reference evapotranspiration minus precipitation, from the typical planting date to the typical harvest date of the tile (Crop calendar). Positive values mean the air demanded more water than fell as rain and snow.

variables.name: gdd
variables.label: Growing degree-days
variables.definition: Sum of the daily mean air temperature above 0 °C from the typical planting date to the typical harvest date of the tile (Crop calendar).

variables.name: ptq
variables.label: Photothermal quotient
variables.definition: Mean solar radiation divided by mean air temperature above 4.5 °C, from 20 days before to 10 days after heading in that season (Crop calendar).

variables.name: hot_days
variables.label: Hot days during grain fill
variables.definition: Number of days with a maximum air temperature of 34 °C or higher from heading to maturity of that season (Crop calendar).

variables.name: emergence
variables.label: Emergence date
variables.definition: Day of emergence in the fall, from the Wang-Engel model calibrated on USDA-NASS crop progress.

variables.name: heading
variables.label: Heading date
variables.definition: Day of heading, from the Wang-Engel model calibrated on USDA-NASS crop progress.

variables.name: maturity
variables.label: Maturity date
variables.definition: Day of maturity, from the Wang-Engel model calibrated on USDA-NASS crop progress.

variables.name: harvest
variables.label: Harvest date
variables.definition: Day of harvest, from the Wang-Engel model calibrated on USDA-NASS crop progress.

variables.name: last_spring_freeze
variables.label: Last spring freeze
variables.definition: Last day from January 1 through June 30 with a minimum air temperature of -2 °C or lower.

variables.name: first_fall_freeze
variables.label: First fall freeze
variables.definition: First day from August 1 with a minimum air temperature of -2 °C or lower, in the fall the crop is sown.

variables.name: cold_snap
variables.label: Fall cold snap
variables.definition: Largest fall of the daily minimum air temperature over 3 days, from the typical planting date of the tile through December 31. Wheat hardens gradually as the fall cools; a sudden plunge can kill plants that have not hardened. Snow cover and soil moisture are not accounted for.

variables.name: coldest_night
variables.label: Coldest night
variables.definition: Lowest daily minimum air temperature from the typical planting date to the typical harvest date of the tile (Crop calendar). Air temperature, not the temperature of the crown: snow cover and soil moisture are not accounted for.

variables.name: deficit_days
variables.label: Deficit-days
variables.definition: Sum of the daily departures of the fraction of available water (FAW, 0 to 60 cm) below 0.5, from the typical planting date to the typical harvest date of the tile. FAW is 0 at the wilting point and 1 at field capacity, so 10 days at a departure of 0.1 make 1 FAW-day. From daily 1-km soil moisture maps of Kansas, averaged over the tile; seasons from 2001-02.

variables.name: surplus_days
variables.label: Surplus-days
variables.definition: Sum of the daily departures of the fraction of available water (FAW, 0 to 60 cm) above 0.5, from the typical planting date to the typical harvest date of the tile. FAW is 0 at the wilting point and 1 at field capacity, so 10 days at a departure of 0.1 make 1 FAW-day. From daily 1-km soil moisture maps of Kansas, averaged over the tile; seasons from 2001-02.

variables.name: spring_deficit_days
variables.label: Spring deficit-days
variables.definition: Sum of the daily departures of the fraction of available water (FAW, 0 to 60 cm) below 0.5, from March 1 through May 31. FAW is 0 at the wilting point and 1 at field capacity, so 10 days at a departure of 0.1 make 1 FAW-day. From daily 1-km soil moisture maps of Kansas, averaged over the tile; seasons from 2001-02.

variables.name: wheat_yield_rainfed
variables.label: Winter wheat yield without irrigation
variables.definition: Non-irrigated yield (USDA-NASS) where published; otherwise the all-practice yield of counties where less than 10% of the harvested wheat was irrigated in 2000-2007.

sources.tiles: Countiles (U.S. county tiles of about 15 x 15 miles, github.com/soilwater/countiles), cut from the U.S. Census Bureau 2023 county boundaries
sources.climate: gridMET (Abatzoglou, 2013), about 4 km daily grids, climatologylab.org/gridmet
sources.wheat: USDA-NASS Quick Stats, county estimates (survey), winter wheat, Kansas: all practices and non-irrigated (1980-2019)
sources.crop calendar: Planting: K-State Kansas Crop Planting Guide (L-818) zones; emergence, heading, maturity and harvest: Wang-Engel phenology model (Wang and Engel, 1998; vernalization of Streck et al., 2003) calibrated on USDA-NASS weekly crop progress for Kansas
sources.soil water: Daily 1-km maps of the fraction of available water, 0-60 cm, and the 1-km map of total available water (kansas-1km project, K-State)
sources.wheat area: USDA-NASS Cropland Data Layer, winter wheat, 2016 to 2023
sources.soil: ISSR-800 soil property grids (USDA-NRCS and UC Davis, from SSURGO/STATSGO), 800 m
